summary: @servicetitan/link-item 41.3.2 executes an obfuscated payload via a dropped Bun runtime at preinstall
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts and chmods the binary under a temp path, and then invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js shipped in the tarball root. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line file whose contents are behind a shuffled string-array decoder (WV8StW rotating a ~1200-entry constant array) and an ASCII substitution table (hc1jfK9); its real behavior is not visible without executing the decoder. Neither setup.mjs nor math_init.js is declared in the package.json "files" array ("dist","src") and neither is referenced by the advertised React link-item component surface. The Bun-under-preinstall invocation path ensures the payload runs outside the Node interpreter that Node-oriented scanners inspect, so the executed bytes bypass the ecosystem's default install-time inspection. The layout — legitimate-looking @servicetitan-scoped React component in src/ and dist/, with an undeclared root-level dropper plus obfuscated blob — matches the pattern of a compromised publish under a trusted scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
